intent.raw_query: Seoul K-culture and food, $2200 couple, winter 2026 from LAX

experiences.name: Gyeongbokgung Palace & Hanbok Experience
experiences.description: Explore the grand Joseon-era Gyeongbokgung Palace while dressed in a traditional Hanbok rental. Wander through historic courtyards, watch the royal guard-changing ceremony, and visit the National Folk Museum of Korea located within the palace grounds. Wearing Hanbok grants free palace entry.

experiences.name: Gwangjang Market Street Food Tour
experiences.description: Dive deep into Seoul's legendary indoor traditional market, one of the oldest in Korea. Sample iconic local dishes including bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak gimbap (addictive mini rice rolls), tteokbokki, and fresh yukhoe (beef tartare). A true feast for food lovers on a budget.

experiences.name: K-Pop Idol Cafe Hopping in Hongdae
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in Seoul's vibrant K-culture scene by exploring the trendy Hongdae district. Visit themed K-pop cafes, browse idol merchandise shops, catch live busking performances by aspiring artists, and explore the colorful street art and indie music culture that defines this youthful neighborhood.

experiences.name: Bukchon Hanok Village Cultural Walk
experiences.description: Stroll through one of Seoul's best-preserved traditional neighborhoods featuring hundreds of restored Hanok (traditional Korean houses). Discover small galleries, tea houses, and craft workshops tucked between narrow alleyways. Enjoy panoramic views of the city skyline contrasted against ancient rooftops — a perfect blend of old and new Korea.

experiences.name: Han River Picnic & Sunset Cruise
experiences.description: Head to Yeouido Hangang Park for a classic Seoul experience — pick up Korean convenience store snacks and chimaek (chicken and beer) from nearby vendors, then relax by the Han River. End the evening with a scenic Han River cruise offering stunning views of Seoul's illuminated skyline and bridges at dusk.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Seoul, South Korea
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Incheon International Airport at 13:00. Take the AREX Airport Express train to Seoul Station (approx. 43 min, ~₩9,500). Transfer to your Gyeongbokgung boutique stay in Jongno-gu. Check in, freshen up, and get oriented with a short walk around the Gyeongbokgung neighborhood to get your bearings.
day_by_day.evening: Gentle first evening stroll along Cheonggyecheon Stream (청계천), a scenic illuminated waterway just a short taxi or bus ride away. Enjoy the winter light installations. Return to Jongno-gu and explore the lively Gwanghwamun area at night.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the plane
meals.lunch: Grab a quick kimbap or convenience store meal (GS25 or CU) at the airport or Seoul Station — under ₩5,000
meals.dinner: Jongno 3-ga Pojangmacha (포장마차) street food stalls near Gwanghwamun: tteokbokki, eomuk (fish cake soup), and hotteok — budget ₩6,000–10,000

day_by_day.notes: Pick up a T-money card at the airport or any convenience store (₩3,000 card + load ₩20,000–30,000). This card covers all subway and bus rides in Seoul. December is cold (0–5°C), so pack thermals and a heavy coat.

day_by_day.morning: Start with a visit to Gyeongbokgung Palace (경복궁) — right on your doorstep! Arrive early (opens 09:00) to beat crowds. Admission: ₩3,000. Watch the Royal Guard Changing Ceremony at 10:00 and 14:00. Rent a hanbok (traditional Korean dress) nearby for ₩15,000–20,000 for free palace entry and great photos.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk through the National Folk Museum of Korea (국립민속박물관) inside the palace grounds — FREE entry. Then stroll through Bukchon Hanok Village (북촌한옥마을), a beautifully preserved traditional village with stunning views. Explore the winding alleys and admire the tile-roofed hanok houses.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Insadong (인사동) for evening shopping — browse traditional crafts, K-culture souvenirs, and street snacks. Visit Ssamziegil, a quirky open-air shopping courtyard. Enjoy the festive winter atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or nearby bakery — Paris Baguette or Tous Les Jours: coffee + pastry ₩4,000–6,000
meals.lunch: Gyeongbokgung area local restaurant: sundubu jjigae (soft tofu stew) set meal ₩8,000–10,000
meals.dinner: Insadong traditional restaurant: bibimbap or doenjang jjigae (fermented soybean paste soup) ₩8,000–12,000

day_by_day.notes: Gyeongbokgung is closed on Tuesdays — but today is Wednesday, so you're fine! Hanbok rental shops are clustered around the palace's east and south gates. Wear warm layers under the hanbok.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Changdeokgung Palace (창덕궁) and its UNESCO-listed Secret Garden (비원/후원). Guided tours of the Secret Garden run at set times — book ahead or join the English tour (10:00 or 14:30). Admission: ₩8,000 (includes garden). A more intimate and romantic palace than Gyeongbokgung.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to nearby Changgyeonggung Palace (창경궁, ₩1,000) and Jongmyo Shrine (종묘, ₩1,000) — a UNESCO World Heritage Site and sacred royal ancestral shrine with a serene, atmospheric feel. Perfect for K-culture and history lovers.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Ikseon-dong (익선동) — Seoul's trendiest retro neighborhood in old hanok houses converted into cafés, cocktail bars, and vintage shops. Very Instagram-worthy and budget-friendly. Try a traditional Korean dessert café.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store breakfast: triangle kimbap + cup ramen or banana milk ₩3,000–5,000
meals.lunch: Local kimbap restaurant near Changdeokgung: kimbap + ramyeon combo ₩5,000–7,000
meals.dinner: Ikseon-dong café-restaurant: Korean fusion or traditional snacks + sikhye (sweet rice drink) ₩10,000–15,000

day_by_day.notes: Jongmyo Shrine is only open to independent visitors on Saturdays — on other days, you must join a guided tour. Check the schedule at the entrance. Ikseon-dong is a 10-minute walk from Jongno 3-ga station.

day_by_day.morning: Take the subway to Namdaemun Market (남대문시장), one of Korea's largest and oldest traditional markets. Browse stalls selling clothes, accessories, Korean snacks, dried seafood, and kitchenware. Great for budget shopping and souvenir hunting. Opens early (some stalls from 06:00).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to nearby Myeongdong (명동) — Seoul's famous shopping and street food district. Sample street foods: hotteok, tornado potato, Korean fried chicken skewers, egg bread (계란빵). Browse cosmetics shops (Innisfree, Etude House, Olive Young) for K-beauty products at great prices.
day_by_day.evening: Visit N Seoul Tower (남산타워) on Namsan Mountain. Take the cable car up (₩13,000 round trip) or hike up for free (30 min). Enjoy panoramic night views of Seoul sparkling in winter. See the famous love locks on the fence.

meals.breakfast: Namdaemun Market: hotteok (sweet pancake) and warm soybean milk (두유) from market stalls ₩2,000–3,000
meals.lunch: Namdaemun Market galchi jorim (braised cutlassfish) or kalguksu (knife-cut noodle soup) ₩7,000–9,000
meals.dinner: Myeongdong street food dinner: mix of skewers, dumplings, and tteokbokki ₩8,000–12,000

day_by_day.notes: Myeongdong is extremely busy on Friday evenings — embrace the energy! Olive Young is the best place for affordable K-beauty products. The cable car to N Seoul Tower may have queues in winter — go before 18:00 or after 20:00 to avoid the longest waits.

day_by_day.morning: Take the subway to Hongdae (홍대) — Seoul's youth culture and indie arts hub. Explore the vibrant street art, murals, and quirky shops around Hongik University. Visit the free Trick Eye Museum area (exterior art is free). Browse vinyl record shops and vintage clothing stores.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short bus ride to Sinchon (신촌) and Yonsei University area — beautiful campus, especially in winter. Then head to the Han River (한강) at Yeouido or Mapo Bridge area for a winter riverside walk. Rent a bicycle (Ttareungi public bike: ₩1,000/hour) if weather permits.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hongdae for the famous Saturday night street performances and busking. K-pop dance crews, indie musicians, and comedians perform on the streets for free. Explore the many affordable bars and pojangmacha tents.

meals.breakfast: Hongdae area bakery or café: croissant + Americano ₩5,000–7,000
meals.lunch: Sinchon local restaurant: dakgalbi (spicy stir-fried chicken) — a Chuncheon specialty popular in Seoul ₩10,000–13,000
meals.dinner: Hongdae street food + cheap pub food: Korean fried chicken (치킨) and beer (chimaek) at a local hof ₩12,000–18,000

day_by_day.notes: Saturday is the best day to visit Hongdae for street performances — they typically start around 18:00–19:00 near the main Hongdae playground area. Ttareungi bikes require a Korean phone number — ask your hostel for help registering if needed.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Gyeonghuigung Palace (경희궁, FREE entry) — a lesser-known, peaceful palace with far fewer tourists. Explore at your own pace. Then walk to the Seoul Museum of History (서울역사박물관, FREE) next door for an excellent overview of Seoul's 600-year history as Korea's capital.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Seodaemun Prison History Hall (서대문형무소역사관, ₩3,000) — a powerful and sobering museum in a former Japanese colonial-era prison that held Korean independence fighters. Important for understanding Korean cultural identity and history.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Sinchon and Edae (이대, Ewha Womans University) area on a Sunday evening — lively with students, affordable restaurants, and K-pop merchandise shops. Browse the underground shopping arcade near Sinchon station.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or local convenience store: dosirak (lunchbox) or egg sandwich ₩3,000–5,000
meals.lunch: Near Seodaemun: haejang-guk (해장국, hangover soup/hearty beef broth) — a Sunday classic ₩8,000–10,000
meals.dinner: Sinchon/Edae area: tteokbokki + sundae (blood sausage) + twigim combo at a bunsik restaurant ₩7,000–10,000

day_by_day.notes: Seodaemun Prison is a deeply emotional site — allow 1.5–2 hours and approach with respect. The museum is especially meaningful for understanding the Korean independence movement and why K-culture places such importance on national identity.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Suwon Hwaseong Fortress (수원화성) — a UNESCO World Heritage fortress just 1 hour from Seoul by subway (Line 1 to Suwon Station, then bus). Walk the full fortress wall circuit (5.7km) for stunning winter views. Admission: ₩1,000. Rent a bicycle inside the fortress grounds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Hwaseong Haenggung Palace (행궁, ₩1,500) inside the fortress — a beautiful royal temporary palace. Watch traditional Korean martial arts or archery demonstrations if scheduled. Explore the surrounding traditional market streets.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Seoul. Relax at your accommodation or take a quiet evening walk through the Gyeongbokgung neighborhood, which is beautifully lit at night in winter.

meals.breakfast: Early convenience store breakfast before departure: triangle kimbap + coffee ₩3,000–4,000
meals.lunch: Suwon's famous galbi (갈비, grilled short ribs) — Suwon galbi is legendary in Korea. Budget set lunch at a local restaurant near the fortress ₩12,000–15,000
meals.dinner: Back in Jongno: simple doenjang jjigae set at a neighborhood restaurant ₩8,000–10,000

day_by_day.notes: Take Line 1 (blue) from Seoul Station directly to Suwon Station (about 55 min, ₩2,050 on T-money). From Suwon Station, take bus 11 or 13 to the fortress. The full wall walk takes 2–3 hours. Dress very warmly — December wind on the fortress walls is biting.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Museum of Korea (국립중앙박물관, FREE) in Yongsan — one of the largest museums in Asia with an extraordinary collection of Korean artifacts, from prehistoric times through the Joseon dynasty. Allow 2–3 hours minimum.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Itaewon (이태원) — Seoul's multicultural district. Browse the eclectic mix of vintage shops, antique markets along Antique Furniture Street, and international food options. Visit Gyeongnidan-gil (경리단길), a trendy uphill street with independent cafés and boutiques.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Haebangchon (HBC, 해방촌) — a charming hillside neighborhood adjacent to Itaewon with a bohemian, artsy vibe. Great for affordable international food and craft beer bars with a local feel.

meals.breakfast: Museum area café or convenience store ₩4,000–6,000
meals.lunch: National Museum of Korea cafeteria: affordable Korean set meals ₩8,000–10,000
meals.dinner: Haebangchon: international budget eats — Turkish döner, Vietnamese pho, or Korean pub snacks ₩10,000–15,000

day_by_day.notes: The National Museum of Korea is closed on Mondays — but today is Tuesday, so you're fine. Take subway Line 4 to Ichon Station (직통) for the museum. Itaewon is a 10-minute walk from Ichon or take Line 6 to Itaewon Station.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Dongdaemun (동대문) area — start at Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP, 동대문디자인플라자), a stunning futuristic building by Zaha Hadid. The exterior and some interior areas are free. Check for any free exhibitions. Browse the surrounding fabric and fashion wholesale markets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Gwangjang Market (광장시장) — one of Seoul's oldest and most beloved traditional markets, famous for its raw fish, mayak kimbap (addictive tiny kimbap rolls), bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), and yukhoe (beef tartare). A food lover's paradise.
day_by_day.evening: Walk along the Cheonggyecheon Stream (청계천) from Gwangjang Market westward toward Gwanghwamun — beautifully lit with winter light festivals. End the evening at a traditional Korean tea house (다방) in Insadong for warm yuja-cha (citron tea).

meals.breakfast: Local bakery near hotel: hotteok or bungeo-ppang (fish-shaped pastry with red bean) from a street cart ₩1,000–2,000
meals.lunch: Gwangjang Market: mayak kimbap + bindaetteok + sikhye ₩8,000–12,000 — eat at the market stalls surrounded by harabeoji and halmoni vendors
meals.dinner: Insadong traditional restaurant: samgyetang (ginseng chicken soup) — warming in winter ₩13,000–15,000

day_by_day.notes: Gwangjang Market is busiest at lunchtime — arrive by 11:30 to get a seat at a stall. The mayak kimbap (마약김밥) literally means 'narcotic kimbap' because it's so addictive — don't miss it! The Cheonggyecheon winter light festival typically runs through January.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Bukhansan National Park (북한산국립공원) for a morning hike — Seoul's stunning mountain national park is accessible by subway (Ui-Sinseol Line to Bukhansan Ui Station). The Dulle-gil trail is a gentle, scenic option. Admission to the park is FREE. Enjoy snow-dusted peaks and fresh mountain air.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the city and visit Jogyesa Temple (조계사) — the head temple of Korean Buddhism, located in Jongno, very close to your hotel. Beautifully decorated with lanterns. Free entry. Attend an afternoon prayer ceremony if one is running. Browse the Buddhist craft shops nearby.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Eve in Seoul! Head to Myeongdong or Hongdae for the festive Christmas atmosphere — Seoul goes all-out with decorations, lights, and events. Many K-pop themed Christmas events and pop-up markets. Enjoy the celebratory street food and the uniquely Korean take on Christmas.

meals.breakfast: Pack a convenience store snack for the hike: onigiri + energy bar + canned coffee ₩4,000–5,000
meals.lunch: Mountain trail snack stall or pack your own: instant ramyeon at a mountain rest stop ₩3,000–4,000
meals.dinner: Christmas Eve treat: Korean BBQ (삼겹살, grilled pork belly) at a local Jongno restaurant — splurge slightly ₩15,000–20,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Bukhansan is accessible but trails can be icy in December — bring hiking poles if possible and wear grippy boots. The Dulle-gil둘레길 trail is the easiest option (flat, 71.5km total but you can do sections). Christmas in Korea is a couples' holiday more than a family one — expect romantic decorations everywhere!

day_by_day.morning: Take the subway to Lotte World (롯데월드) in Jamsil — one of the world's largest indoor theme parks. Christmas Day will have special decorations and events. Admission: ₩62,000 (full day). Alternatively, the Magic Island outdoor section and Lotte World Mall are free to browse if on a tighter budget.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Seokchon Lake (석촌호수) adjacent to Lotte World — a beautiful free park with a scenic lake. Walk around the lake and enjoy the winter landscape. Then visit the nearby Lotte World Tower Sky31 observation deck (₩27,000) for spectacular 360° views of Seoul from 500m high — or skip for budget reasons.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Gangnam (강남) for the evening — walk along Garosu-gil (가로수길), a tree-lined boulevard with boutique shops and cafés. Experience the upscale side of Seoul that BTS and K-pop videos made famous. Window shop and enjoy the atmosphere without spending much.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or nearby café: warm porridge (죽, juk) — a Korean Christmas morning comfort ₩6,000–8,000
meals.lunch: Jamsil area: Korean fast food chain like Lotteria or Isaac Toast for a budget Christmas lunch ₩5,000–8,000
meals.dinner: Gangnam: affordable Korean BBQ chain restaurant (like Palsaik or Gen Korean BBQ) — Christmas dinner Korean style ₩15,000–20,000

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Day is a public holiday in South Korea (one of the few predominantly non-Christian countries where it is). Many attractions are open. Lotte World is very popular — book tickets online in advance. Garosu-gil is about a 10-minute walk from Sinnonhyeon Station (Line 9).

day_by_day.morning: Visit the War Memorial of Korea (전쟁기념관, FREE) in Yongsan — a vast and impressive museum documenting Korean military history from ancient times through the Korean War. Outdoor exhibits include tanks, aircraft, and warships. Allow 2–3 hours. Essential for understanding modern Korean identity.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Yeouido (여의도) — Seoul's financial and broadcasting district. Visit the KBS (Korean Broadcasting System) building area — home of many K-pop music shows. Walk along the Yeouido Hangang Park riverside. If you're a K-pop fan, check if any music show recordings are happening (KBS Music Bank airs Fridays, but Saturday rehearsals sometimes occur).
day_by_day.evening: Final Saturday night out in Seoul: return to Hongdae for a farewell evening of street performances, K-pop in the clubs, and street food. Alternatively, visit a norebang (노래방, Korean karaoke room) for a quintessential K-culture experience — typically ₩10,000–15,000 per hour per room.

meals.breakfast: Yongsan area: Korean breakfast set at a local restaurant — doenjang jjigae + rice + banchan ₩7,000–9,000
meals.lunch: War Memorial area: nearby local restaurant: kimchi jjigae (김치찌개) set ₩8,000–10,000
meals.dinner: Hongdae: Korean fried chicken (yangnyeom chicken) + beer at a local chimaek restaurant ₩13,000–18,000

day_by_day.notes: The War Memorial of Korea is one of the most impressive free museums in Seoul — don't skip it. For K-pop music show tickets (KBS Music Bank, MBC Show! Music Core, SBS Inkigayo), you typically need to apply online weeks in advance through fan clubs, but it's worth checking for last-minute openings.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — revisit your favorite neighborhood near Gyeongbokgung for a leisurely farewell walk. Stop by a local Korean café for a slow breakfast. Visit any last-minute spots you missed, such as the National Palace Museum of Korea (국립고궁박물관, FREE) adjacent to Gyeongbokgung.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping at Insadong or Namdaemun Market. Stock up on Korean snacks, instant ramyeon, K-beauty products, and traditional crafts for gifts. Pack your bags and check out. Head to Seoul Station for the AREX Airport Express to Incheon (departs regularly, ~43 min, ₩9,500).
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Incheon International Airport. Reflect on 13 incredible days of K-culture, traditional palaces, street food, and the vibrant energy of Seoul.

meals.breakfast: Favorite local café near Gyeongbokgung: slow farewell breakfast — dalgona coffee + patbingsu or Korean pastry ₩6,000–9,000
meals.lunch: Insadong area: last Korean meal — bulgogi (불고기) rice set or jajangmyeon (black bean noodles) ₩9,000–12,000
meals.dinner: Airport: Incheon Airport has excellent Korean food options — try a final bowl of kimchi ramen or Korean set meal in the departure lounge ₩10,000–15,000

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before your flight for the AREX journey + airport check-in and security. The AREX City Airport Terminal at Seoul Station allows you to check in your luggage and go through immigration before heading to the airport — highly recommended to save time. Keep some won for last-minute purchases but note that unused won can be exchanged back at the airport.

trip_options.title: Classic Seoul, South Korea Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – In transit. Flight LH lands at Incheon International Airport at 13:00.
day_by_day.afternoon: Clear immigration and customs, collect baggage, then take the AREX Express Train (~43 min) or Airport Limousine Bus to central Seoul. Check in to your Boutique Stay in Gyeongbokgung, Jongno-gu. Freshen up and take a gentle orientation stroll around the Gyeongbokgung Palace walls and nearby Bukchon Hanok Village alleys to get your bearings.
day_by_day.evening: Ease into Seoul with a relaxed walk along Insadong-gil street, browsing traditional craft shops and galleries. Head to Insadong Ssamziegil courtyard for a warm drink and light snacks from street vendors.

meals.breakfast: On the plane.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at Incheon Airport food court – try a bowl of Bibimbap or Tteokbokki (~₩10,000–15,000).
meals.dinner: Tosokchon Samgyetang (토속촌 삼계탕) near Gyeongbokgung – famous ginseng chicken soup, perfect for warming up after travel (~₩18,000–22,000 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Jet lag tip: stay awake until at least 21:00 local time to adjust faster. Get T-money card at the airport or any convenience store for seamless subway/bus travel.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Gyeongbokgung Palace (경복궁) right at your doorstep – arrive early (~09:00) to catch the Royal Guard Changing Ceremony (held at 10:00 and 14:00). Explore the main palace grounds and Gyeonghoeru Pavilion. Consider renting a Hanbok at a nearby shop for free or discounted entry.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk north to the National Folk Museum of Korea (inside the palace grounds, free entry with palace ticket). Then head to Bukchon Hanok Village for a self-guided walking tour through traditional Korean wooden houses with stunning views of the city.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Samcheong-dong street – charming boutiques, art galleries, and cafés. Wind down at a traditional tea house with Omija (五味子) berry tea or Sikhye rice punch.

meals.breakfast: Café or convenience store near hotel – triangle kimbap, egg sandwich, and coffee (~₩5,000–8,000).
meals.lunch: Gwanghwamun Gukbap (광화문국밥) – hearty pork soup with rice, a local lunch staple (~₩10,000–13,000).
meals.dinner: Samcheong-dong Sujebi – hand-torn noodle soup restaurant in the area (~₩12,000–15,000).

day_by_day.notes: Gyeongbokgung is closed on Tuesdays – since today is Wednesday, it's fully open. Dress warmly; December in Seoul is cold (0°C to -5°C). Hanbok rental shops are clustered around the palace's east gate.

day_by_day.morning: Take the subway to Changdeokgung Palace (창덕궁) and book the Secret Garden (Huwon) guided tour – a stunning UNESCO-listed rear garden. Tours run at set times and must be reserved online in advance.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to nearby Changgyeonggung Palace and then to the National Museum of Korea in Yongsan (30 min by subway) – one of Asia's largest museums with free admission. Explore Korean history from prehistoric times to the Joseon dynasty.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Itaewon for a cosmopolitan evening vibe. Browse the main strip and side streets, then settle in for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel area café – Hotteok (sweet pancake) from a street stall and coffee (~₩3,000–6,000).
meals.lunch: Jongno 3-ga area – visit Gwangjang Market for street food lunch: Mayak Kimbap, Bindaetteok (mung bean pancake), and Yukhoe (beef tartare) (~₩10,000–15,000).
meals.dinner: Itaewon – try a mid-range Korean BBQ restaurant; Maple Tree House or similar for quality Galbi and Samgyeopsal (~₩25,000–35,000 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Book the Changdeokgung Secret Garden tour online at least a day ahead – spots fill up quickly even in winter. The National Museum of Korea is free and well worth 2–3 hours.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Insadong in depth – visit the Unhyeongung Royal Residence (small, uncrowded palace), then browse antique shops, traditional paper (hanji) stores, and indie bookshops along the main street.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP) – the futuristic Zaha Hadid-designed cultural complex. Explore the design museum and any current exhibitions. Walk around Dongdaemun Market area.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Dongdaemun's famous night shopping scene. The wholesale fashion markets (Doota, Migliore) come alive after 20:00. Browse fashion, accessories, and street food stalls.

meals.breakfast: Insadong Café – traditional Sikhye and Yaksik (sweet rice cake) breakfast at a hanok café (~₩7,000–10,000).
meals.lunch: Insadong area – Bibimbap at a cozy local restaurant (~₩12,000–15,000).
meals.dinner: Dongdaemun street food crawl – Tteokbokki, Sundae (blood sausage), Eomuk (fish cake skewers), Hotteok (~₩10,000–15,000 total).

day_by_day.notes: DDP has rotating exhibitions – check their website for current shows. Dongdaemun is best visited in the evening when the neon lights and market energy peak. Wear comfortable walking shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Bukhansan National Park (북한산) – take the subway to Gupabal or Dobongsan station and hike one of the trails. The Baegundae Peak trail offers stunning winter views (3–4 hours round trip, moderate difficulty).
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the city and visit Seodaemun Prison History Hall (서대문형무소역사관) – a powerful museum documenting the Japanese colonial period and Korean independence movement.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Hongdae (홍대) neighborhood – the vibrant university arts district. Catch live street performances (busking), browse indie boutiques, and soak in the youthful K-culture energy.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store near trailhead – Onigiri, banana milk, and instant coffee (~₩5,000).
meals.lunch: Post-hike meal at a local Doenjang Jjigae (fermented soybean stew) restaurant near Bukhansan (~₩10,000–13,000).
meals.dinner: Hongdae – try Gopchang (grilled intestines) or Dakgalbi (spicy stir-fried chicken) at a lively local spot (~₩15,000–20,000 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Wear proper hiking boots and layer up – Bukhansan in December can be icy on trails. Crampons (아이젠) are sold/rented at the trailhead. Seodaemun Prison is closed on Mondays.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Jogyesa Temple (조계사) – the head temple of Korean Buddhism, beautifully decorated with lanterns. Attend a morning ceremony if timing allows. Then explore the nearby Cheonggyecheon Stream for a peaceful winter walk.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Gyeonghuigung Palace (경희궁) – a quieter, less-visited palace. Then visit the Seoul Museum of History next door (free admission) for a deep dive into the city's evolution.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Gwanghwamun Square and the surrounding area at night, beautifully lit in winter. Walk to nearby청계광장 (Cheonggye Plaza) for the winter light festival displays.

meals.breakfast: Near Jogyesa Temple – traditional temple-style vegetarian breakfast at a nearby Buddhist café (~₩8,000–12,000).
meals.lunch: Cheonggyecheon area – Haejangguk (hangover soup/ox bone soup) at a local restaurant (~₩12,000–15,000).
meals.dinner: Gwanghwamun area – Jungsik or a mid-range Korean cuisine restaurant; try Japchae (glass noodles) and Jeon (savory pancakes) (~₩20,000–28,000 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Jogyesa Temple often has beautiful winter lantern displays in December. The Cheonggyecheon Stream winter light festival (Seoul Lantern Festival aftermath decorations) may still be partially up – check local listings.

day_by_day.morning: Take the subway to Gangnam (강남) – visit COEX Mall and the famous COEX Starfield Library (별마당 도서관), an Instagram-worthy open library inside the mall. Browse Gangnam's upscale streets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the SM Entertainment flagship store and SM Town Museum (if open) for a K-pop deep dive. Head to Apgujeong Rodeo Street and Garosu-gil (가로수길) – Seoul's most stylish shopping boulevard lined with boutiques and cafés.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Gangnam nightlife at a rooftop bar or visit a Norebang (노래방 – private karaoke room) for a quintessential K-culture evening activity.

meals.breakfast: Hotel area – simple Korean breakfast of Congee (Juk) from a nearby Juk restaurant (~₩8,000–10,000).
meals.lunch: COEX food court or Gangnam area – Kimchi Jjigae set meal (~₩12,000–15,000).
meals.dinner: Garosu-gil – trendy mid-range restaurant; try Korean fusion cuisine or a modern Hansik (Korean cuisine) restaurant (~₩25,000–35,000 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Norebang rooms are typically ₩15,000–25,000/hour for a private room. Gangnam is pricier than northern Seoul – budget accordingly. Apgujeong is a great area for K-beauty product shopping.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Lotte World Tower and Sky100 Observatory (롯데월드타워) in Jamsil for panoramic views of Seoul. The observation deck on the 100th floor offers incredible winter cityscape views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Lotte World Amusement Park (if interested) or head to Olympic Park (올림픽공원) nearby – a beautiful large park with outdoor sculptures and the KSPO Dome. Visit the Seoul Olympic Museum.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Seongsu-dong (성수동) – Seoul's hippest up-and-coming neighborhood, nicknamed 'Seoul's Brooklyn.' Explore converted factory spaces, concept stores, and artisan cafés.

meals.breakfast: Jamsil area – Egg drop sandwich café or Paris Baguette for a Western-Korean fusion breakfast (~₩7,000–10,000).
meals.lunch: Olympic Park area – packed lunch from a convenience store or nearby Gimbap restaurant (~₩8,000–12,000).
meals.dinner: Seongsu-dong – trendy restaurant in a converted warehouse; try craft burgers, artisan pizza, or modern Korean cuisine (~₩20,000–28,000 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Sky100 Observatory ticket is ~₩27,000. Book online for a discount. Seongsu-dong is best explored on foot – the area around Ttukseom station is the most vibrant.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Suwon (수원) – take the subway/train (~1 hour). Visit Hwaseong Fortress (화성), a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Walk the full 5.7km fortress wall circuit for stunning views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Suwon's Hwaseong Haenggung Palace and the surrounding traditional market. Visit the Suwon Hwaseong Museum to learn about the fortress's history.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Seoul and spend the evening at Namdaemun Market (남대문시장) – one of Korea's oldest and largest traditional markets. Great for souvenirs, clothing, and street food.

meals.breakfast: Hotel area – quick Korean breakfast at a nearby Gimbap Cheonguk (김밥천국) chain restaurant (~₩5,000–8,000).
meals.lunch: Suwon Galbi (수원갈비) – Suwon is famous for its large-cut beef ribs; enjoy at a local restaurant near Hwaseong (~₩20,000–30,000 per person).
meals.dinner: Namdaemun Market street food – Hotteok, Haemul Pajeon (seafood pancake), and grilled skewers (~₩10,000–15,000).

day_by_day.notes: Hwaseong Fortress entry is ~₩1,000. The walk is beautiful but cold – dress in warm layers. Namdaemun Market is busiest in the evening and is great for buying Korean snacks as gifts.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Namsan Seoul Tower (N Seoul Tower / 남산타워) – take the cable car up Namsan Mountain. Enjoy the iconic love locks and panoramic winter views of the city. Explore Namsan Park.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Myeongdong (명동) – Seoul's busiest shopping district. Browse K-beauty brands (Innisfree, Etude House, Olive Young), fashion stores, and street food vendors. Stock up on skincare and cosmetics.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Eve in Seoul is festive and romantic. Myeongdong Cathedral (명동성당) holds special Christmas Eve Mass – a beautiful cultural experience. The area is decorated with lights and markets.

meals.breakfast: Hotel area – warm Porridge (Hobak Juk – pumpkin porridge) from a Juk café (~₩8,000–10,000).
meals.lunch: Myeongdong street food – Cheese Lobster, Giant Crab, Tteokbokki, and Korean corn dogs (~₩12,000–18,000).
meals.dinner: Special Christmas Eve dinner – try a mid-range Korean course meal (Hanjeongsik) at a restaurant near Myeongdong (~₩35,000–50,000 per person).

day_by_day.notes: N Seoul Tower cable car is ~₩12,000 round trip. Christmas Eve in Myeongdong is extremely crowded but magical. Book dinner reservations in advance as restaurants fill up quickly on Christmas Eve.

day_by_day.morning: Christmas Day is a public holiday in South Korea. Visit Deoksugung Palace (덕수궁) – the only palace open on Mondays (and holidays). Enjoy the Guard Changing Ceremony and the adjacent Deoksugung Doldam-gil stone wall path.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Seoul Museum of Art (SeMA) next to Deoksugung – often has excellent contemporary Korean art exhibitions. Then walk to Cheonggyecheon Stream for a peaceful holiday stroll.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Bukchon Hanok Village at night for a magical winter atmosphere with traditional lanterns. End the evening at a cozy pojangmacha (포장마차 – street tent bar) for Makgeolli (rice wine) and Anju (bar snacks).

meals.breakfast: Hotel area – Christmas morning treat at a bakery; try a Korean-style cream bread and café latte (~₩8,000–12,000).
meals.lunch: Deoksugung area – Seolleongtang (ox bone soup) at a traditional restaurant, perfect for a cold Christmas Day (~₩13,000–16,000).
meals.dinner: Insadong or Jongno area – Jjimdak (braised soy chicken) or Dakdoritang (spicy chicken stew) at a cozy restaurant (~₩18,000–25,000 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Many shops and some restaurants may have reduced hours on Christmas Day – plan ahead. Deoksugung's stone wall path (Doldam-gil) is one of Seoul's most romantic winter walks.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the War Memorial of Korea (전쟁기념관) in Yongsan – a comprehensive and moving museum covering Korean military history and the Korean War. Free admission to most exhibits.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Yongsan Electronics Market (용산전자상가) – Asia's largest electronics market. Browse gadgets, K-pop merchandise, and tech accessories. Then explore nearby Haebangchon (HBC) – a charming hillside neighborhood with multicultural cafés and indie bars.
day_by_day.evening: Final major shopping evening – return to Myeongdong or visit Times Square Mall in Yeongdeungpo for last-minute gift shopping. Enjoy a farewell walk along the Han River at Yeouido for winter night views.

meals.breakfast: Yongsan area – Korean-style breakfast at a local restaurant; Doenjang Jjigae set with rice and banchan (~₩9,000–12,000).
meals.lunch: Haebangchon – multicultural lunch at a local café or international restaurant (~₩12,000–18,000).
meals.dinner: Yeouido area – Samgyeopsal BBQ dinner at a lively Korean BBQ restaurant; grill your own pork belly at the table (~₩18,000–25,000 per person).

day_by_day.notes: The War Memorial of Korea is free and takes 2–3 hours to explore properly. Haebangchon is a great area for unique, non-touristy cafés popular with expats and locals alike.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning – return to any favorite spots or pick up last-minute items. Visit a nearby jjimjilbang (찜질방 – Korean sauna/spa) such as Dragon Hill Spa for a traditional Korean spa experience before departure. Soak in hot baths, use the heated rooms, and relax.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the hotel (store luggage if needed). Final stroll through Gyeongbokgung area and Insadong for any last souvenir shopping. Head to the airport with plenty of time – take AREX from Seoul Station (~43 min to Incheon).
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Incheon International Airport. Enjoy duty-free shopping for Korean snacks, cosmetics, and gifts before boarding.

meals.breakfast: Jjimjilbang – traditional hard-boiled eggs (맥반석 계란) and Sikhye (sweet rice drink) inside the spa (~₩3,000–5,000 extra).
meals.lunch: Final Korean meal – Naengmyeon (cold buckwheat noodles) or Sundubu Jjigae (soft tofu stew) at a local restaurant near the hotel (~₩12,000–15,000).
meals.dinner: Incheon Airport – wide variety of Korean and international dining options in the departure terminal (~₩15,000–25,000).

day_by_day.notes: Dragon Hill Spa (용산) entry is ~₩12,000–15,000. Allow at least 3 hours before your flight for check-in, security, and immigration at Incheon. The airport has excellent duty-free stores for Korean beauty products, snacks (Pepero, Choco Pie, Honey Butter Chips), and ginseng products.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Seoul, South Korea Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Incheon International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged from ICN to boutique stay in Gyeongbokgung, Jongno-gu (approx. 60–70 min via chauffeured sedan). Check-in, unpack, and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle orientation stroll through the Bukchon Hanok Village, just a short walk from the hotel. Admire the traditional Korean hanok architecture, narrow stone-paved alleys, and sweeping views toward Gyeongbokgung Palace. Stop at a curated local craft shop to pick up a small welcome-to-Seoul keepsake.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Mingles (Gangnam) or, closer to the hotel, Jungsik Seoul — one of Korea's most celebrated fine-dining restaurants blending modern Korean cuisine with classical techniques. Pair with a curated Korean natural wine or premium makgeolli flight.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight meal
meals.lunch: Light snack or airport lounge refreshments at ICN
meals.dinner: Jungsik Seoul — modern Korean tasting menu (approx. KRW 250,000–350,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance. Keep Day 1 light to recover from long-haul flight. Hotel concierge can assist with dinner reservations upon arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Royal morning at Gyeongbokgung Palace, steps from the hotel. Arrive early for the Royal Guard Changing Ceremony (10:00 & 14:00). Opt for a private English-speaking guide to unlock the palace's Joseon Dynasty history. Visit the National Folk Museum of Korea within the palace grounds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Insadong, Seoul's premier traditional arts and antiques district. Browse galleries, ceramics studios, and specialty tea houses. Visit Ssamziegil — a charming courtyard mall featuring local artisan goods, handmade jewelry, and K-culture collectibles. Enjoy a premium traditional tea ceremony at O'Sulloc Tea House Insadong.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Tosokchon Samgyetang (iconic ginseng chicken soup, a Seoul institution) for a cultural culinary experience, followed by a night stroll along the illuminated Cheonggyecheon Stream nearby.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast — traditional Korean morning spread (doenjang jjigae, banchan, rice, and fresh fruit)
meals.lunch: Balwoo Gongyang — award-winning Buddhist temple cuisine in Insadong (vegetarian, meditative dining experience)
meals.dinner: Tosokchon Samgyetang — premium private room booking recommended

day_by_day.notes: Gyeongbokgung Palace is walkable from the hotel. Wear comfortable shoes for cobblestone paths. Book Balwoo Gongyang well in advance — reservations fill up quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of Changdeokgung Palace and its UNESCO-listed Secret Garden (Huwon). The Secret Garden is especially atmospheric in December with frost-dusted pavilions and bare ancient trees. Limited daily entry — book tickets in advance.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the National Museum of Korea in Yongsan for a deep dive into Korean art, history, and culture across 5,000 years. The museum's collection of Goryeo celadon and Joseon-era paintings is world-class. Enjoy the museum café overlooking the sculpture garden.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at La Yeon (The Shilla Hotel) — three-Michelin-starred Korean fine dining with panoramic city views. One of Seoul's most prestigious dining experiences, featuring seasonal ingredients prepared in royal court tradition.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: National Museum of Korea café — light Korean-Western fusion bites
meals.dinner: La Yeon, The Shilla Seoul — royal Korean tasting menu (reserve 4–6 weeks in advance; approx. KRW 300,000–450,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Secret Garden tours are guided only and run on a fixed schedule. Book online in advance. La Yeon requires formal attire.

day_by_day.morning: Immersive K-culture morning: visit the National Hangeul Museum near Yongsan to explore the origin and beauty of the Korean alphabet. Then head to the Korean Cultural Heritage Foundation for a private hands-on hanji (Korean paper) or najeonchilgi (mother-of-pearl lacquerware) craft workshop.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Ikseon-dong Hanok Village — a hip, beautifully preserved neighborhood of converted hanok houses now home to specialty coffee shops, dessert bars, and boutique lifestyle stores. Visit a premium omakase dessert café for Korean-style patisserie.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a live performance at the National Theater of Korea — check December 2027 schedule for traditional Korean performing arts (gugak, pansori, or court dance). The theater sits beautifully at the foot of Namsan Mountain.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Ikseon-dong — lunch at Ikseon Galbi, a premium Korean short-rib restaurant in a restored hanok
meals.dinner: Pre- or post-show dinner at Gaon (3 Michelin stars) — Korean royal cuisine in a serene, minimalist setting

day_by_day.notes: Book National Theater tickets well in advance. Gaon is one of only a handful of restaurants in Korea with three Michelin stars — reservations are essential months ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the UNESCO World Heritage village of Yangdong Folk Village or Namsangol Hanok Village (closer option, within Seoul). Namsangol offers a living recreation of Joseon-era life with five restored aristocratic and commoner hanok homes, traditional games, and cultural performances.
day_by_day.afternoon: Ascend Namsan Tower (N Seoul Tower) via cable car for sweeping 360° winter panoramas of Seoul. Visit the observation deck and the Locks of Love installation. Explore the surrounding Namsan Park forest trails — serene and uncrowded in winter.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Myeongdong — visit Myeongdong Kyoja for premium handmade knife-cut noodles (kalguksu) and dumplings, a Seoul culinary landmark. Afterward, browse Myeongdong's evening street food stalls for tteokbokki, hotteok, and Korean corn dogs.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Namsangol Hanok Village traditional food experience — dosirak (Korean bento) picnic or on-site restaurant
meals.dinner: Myeongdong Kyoja — premium noodle and dumpling dinner; supplement with Myeongdong street food

day_by_day.notes: Namsan cable car may have queues on weekends — consider going early afternoon. Dress warmly for outdoor Namsan activities in December.

day_by_day.morning: Private Korean cooking class with a renowned chef — learn to prepare kimchi, japchae, galbi, and doenjang jjigae using premium seasonal ingredients. Classes often held in Jongno or Mapo districts and include a market visit to Gwangjang Market for ingredient sourcing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Gwangjang Market (one of Korea's oldest traditional markets) post-class. Sample bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak gimbap (addictive sesame rice rolls), and yukhoe (beef tartare) from legendary stalls. Browse vintage Korean textiles and silks on the upper floors.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset and evening at Bukhansan National Park's southern trailhead viewpoint (accessible by taxi), then dinner back in the Jongno area at Sanchon — a celebrated temple food restaurant known for its elegant vegetarian Korean cuisine and traditional music performances.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Gwangjang Market — curated street food tasting experience
meals.dinner: Sanchon, Insadong — temple cuisine with live traditional music (approx. KRW 60,000–80,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the private cooking class at least one week in advance. Gwangjang Market is most vibrant on weekends. Sanchon performances typically begin at 19:30.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Suwon Hwaseong Fortress (1 hour south of Seoul by KTX or private car) — a stunning UNESCO-listed late Joseon fortress wall with watchtowers, gates, and military command posts. Walk the full 5.7km perimeter for dramatic winter views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Hwaseong Haenggung (temporary palace) within the fortress grounds and watch the traditional Royal Military Guard performance (check seasonal schedule). Return to Seoul by mid-afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Premium jjimjilbang (Korean bathhouse spa) experience at Spa Lei or Dragon Hill Spa — indulge in hot mineral pools, jimjilbang rooms, body scrub (Italy towel exfoliation), and relaxation lounges. A quintessential Korean wellness ritual.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Suwon Galbi — Suwon is famous for its thick-cut beef short ribs; dine at a traditional galbi restaurant near the fortress
meals.dinner: Light spa-side dining at Dragon Hill Spa's restaurant, or return to Jongno for dinner at Dooreyoo — creative Korean cuisine by a celebrated local chef

day_by_day.notes: Private car hire recommended for Suwon day trip for comfort and flexibility. Book spa in advance for peak December evenings.

day_by_day.morning: Immerse in Seoul's contemporary art scene: visit the Leeum Samsung Museum of Art in Hannam-dong — one of Asia's finest private art museums, housing Korean national treasures alongside works by Damien Hirst, Jeff Koons, and Anish Kapoor in a stunning building by three world-renowned architects.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Hannam-dong and Itaewon — Seoul's most cosmopolitan neighborhood. Browse premium concept stores (Gentle Monster flagship, Ader Error), international designer boutiques, and bespoke Korean menswear ateliers. Visit the Antique Furniture Street for Korean celadon and antique collecting.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Dote on Hannam — an intimate, reservation-only Korean fine dining experience, or Tartine Manufactory Seoul for a globally celebrated bakery-restaurant hybrid with Korean-inflected seasonal menus.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Hannam-dong — lunch at Vatos Urban Tacos (Korean-Mexican fusion, a Seoul cult favorite) or Pierre's Brasserie at Hôtel de la Paix
meals.dinner: Dote on Hannam or Onjium — contemporary Korean cuisine with deep cultural research behind every dish (Michelin-recommended)

day_by_day.notes: Leeum Museum may have temporary exhibitions in December 2027 — check schedule. Hannam-dong is best explored on foot.

day_by_day.morning: K-pop and Korean Wave cultural deep dive: visit the HYBE Insight Museum in Yongsan — an immersive exhibition dedicated to BTS and the global K-pop phenomenon, featuring costumes, behind-the-scenes content, and interactive installations. Book timed entry tickets well in advance.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Hongdae (Hongik University area) — the epicenter of Seoul's indie music, street art, and youth culture. Explore record shops, K-pop merchandise stores, vintage clothing boutiques, and live music venues. Catch a free street performance if available.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a live K-pop showcase, indie concert, or nanta performance (check December 2027 listings). Dinner in Hongdae at Maple Tree House — premium Korean BBQ with USDA prime and Hanwoo beef in an upscale setting.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Hongdae — lunch at Yeonnam-dong's charming café district; try Anthracite Coffee Roasters for specialty coffee and artisan sandwiches
meals.dinner: Maple Tree House, Hongdae — premium Korean BBQ (Hanwoo beef; approx. KRW 150,000–250,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: HYBE Insight tickets sell out weeks in advance — book online immediately. Hongdae is most vibrant in the late afternoon and evening.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Bukchon and Seochon Hanok Village areas in depth — hire a private cultural guide for a two-hour walking tour covering hidden alleyways, historic aristocratic residences, and the stories of the artists and scholars who lived here during the Joseon period.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Gyeonghuigung Palace (less-visited, serene) and the Seoul Museum of History nearby. Afterward, browse Tongin Market — a charming traditional market where you can use old copper coins to select banchan dishes and create your own Korean lunch tray.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Eve special dinner: book a premium hotel restaurant such as Akira Back at JW Marriott or Dining in Space at Signiel Seoul (floors 76–81 of Lotte World Tower) for an extraordinary Christmas Eve tasting menu with panoramic night views of Seoul.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Tongin Market dosirak (coin-operated banchan lunch) — a unique and affordable cultural experience
meals.dinner: Dining in Space, Signiel Seoul — Christmas Eve special menu with city panorama (reserve months in advance)

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Eve in Seoul is festive and romantic — streets are decorated and couples celebrate widely. Book Christmas Eve dinner 2–3 months in advance. Signiel Seoul observation dining is a once-in-a-trip experience.

day_by_day.morning: Peaceful Christmas morning: visit Jogyesa Temple, the head temple of Korean Buddhism in central Seoul, beautifully decorated with lanterns. Attend a morning ceremony or simply meditate in the tranquil courtyard. Explore the temple's cultural museum.
day_by_day.afternoon: Winter experience at Lotte World or COEX Aquarium area in Jamsil — alternatively, visit the Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP) for its futuristic Zaha Hadid-designed architecture and a special Christmas design exhibition or market.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas dinner at Château de Jongno or Bicena — a French-Korean fusion fine dining restaurant, or opt for an in-hotel premium Christmas set dinner. End the evening with a stroll along the beautifully lit Cheonggyecheon Stream and Gwanghwamun Square Christmas installations.

meals.breakfast: Festive Christmas brunch at the hotel or at Grand Hyatt Seoul's Christmas brunch buffet (book in advance)
meals.lunch: Light café lunch at DDP's on-site café or nearby Euljiro specialty coffee district
meals.dinner: Bicena or hotel Christmas set menu — premium French-Korean tasting menu

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Day in Seoul is a public holiday. Most palaces and some museums may have altered hours — confirm in advance. Cheonggyecheon Stream is especially beautiful with winter lights.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nami Island (Namiseom) and Petite France — a scenic 90-minute private car journey to this iconic crescent-shaped island, famous for its tree-lined avenues, winter birch forests, and serene riverside atmosphere. Rent a bicycle and explore at leisure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Petite France cultural village nearby — a quirky French-themed cultural park on a hillside above the North Han River, featuring exhibits on Antoine de Saint-Exupéry and The Little Prince, traditional French architecture, and panoramic lake views. Return to Seoul by early evening.
day_by_day.evening: Final premium shopping evening in Gangnam — visit the luxury boutiques of Apgujeong Rodeo Street (Louis Vuitton, Chanel, Hermès) and the Galleria Department Store luxury wing. Dinner at Garosugil's acclaimed restaurant strip.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast or early departure snack box prepared by hotel
meals.lunch: Nami Island — riverside café lunch with seasonal Korean dishes
meals.dinner: Garosugil, Gangnam — dinner at Mosu Seoul (Michelin-starred, creative Korean-Californian cuisine) or Plant (premium plant-based Korean)

day_by_day.notes: Private car hire strongly recommended for Nami Island day trip. Weekend traffic can extend travel time — depart by 08:30. Bring warm layers; Nami Island is colder than central Seoul in December.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely final morning in Seoul. Enjoy a slow, indulgent hotel breakfast. Take a last contemplative walk through Gyeongbokgung Palace's outer walls and Gwanghwamun Square as the palace opens for the day. Visit a nearby specialty coffee roaster (Fritz Coffee Company or Namusairo) for a final Seoul espresso.
day_by_day.afternoon: Departure preparation: check out of hotel, collect any last-minute souvenirs from Insadong or the hotel gift shop (premium Korean teas, hanji goods, ginseng products, or Korean beauty sets). Private luxury transfer to Incheon International Airport — allow 90 minutes minimum for December weekend traffic.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Incheon International Airport. Enjoy the premium airport lounges (Korean Air Prestige Lounge or Asiana Business Lounge) with Korean cuisine and duty-free shopping before boarding.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent final hotel breakfast — full Korean and Western spread
meals.lunch: Light farewell lunch at a Jongno café, or early airport lounge dining
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dinner or in-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Check hotel checkout time and arrange late checkout if needed (usually until 14:00 for premium guests). Confirm private airport transfer the evening before. Incheon Airport duty-free is world-class — budget time for last-minute Korean skincare, spirits, and confectionery shopping.

query: Seoul K-culture and food, $2200 couple, winter 2026 from LAX
